name.text: Shared: Find the interval of values that round to a target

questiontext.text:
A whole number rounds to \[ {@rounded_value@} \] when rounded to the nearest {@place_name@}.

What is the smallest whole number that could have produced this rounded value?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

What is the largest whole number that could have produced this rounded value?

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

The rounded result is \[ {@rounded_value@} \] to the nearest {@place_name@}.

The lower boundary is halfway between this rounded value and the previous multiple: \[ {@lower_answer@}. \]

The upper halfway value would round to the next multiple under the half-up rule, so the largest whole number in this interval is one less: \[ {@upper_answer@}. \]

Therefore the possible whole numbers are \[ \boxed{ {@lower_answer@} \text{ through } {@upper_answer@} }. \]

reverse-rounding-interval

Learners identify the smallest and largest whole numbers that round to a specified target value.

Targets the belief that a rounded value corresponds to only one original number, and checks understanding of the upper halfway boundary.

Original STACK question. No external wording or mathematical content is copied.

None.

Curriculum alignment is maintained outside the question source.

prtcorrect.text: Correct. A rounded result represents an interval of possible original values.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: One boundary is correct. Recheck the halfway points around the rounded value.

prtincorrect.text: A rounded value can represent many different original numbers.

node.description: Lower boundary is correct. Checks the upper boundary.

truefeedback.text: Correct. You identified the complete whole-number interval.

node.description: Checks whether the learner assumes the rounded value is the only possible original value.

falsefeedback.text: Find the halfway point between this rounded value and the previous multiple.

node.description: Checks whether the upper halfway boundary was incorrectly included.

truefeedback.text:
You included the upper halfway value.

Under the half-up rule, that exact halfway value rounds to the next higher multiple, so the largest whole number in this interval is one less.

node.description: Checks whether both boundaries were set equal to the rounded result.

truefeedback.text:
A rounded result does not identify one unique original value.

There is a whole interval of values that round to the same result.

falsefeedback.text: Find both boundary values around the rounded target.

qtest.description: Correct lower and upper boundaries receive full credit.
Assuming the rounded result is the only possible original value receives zero credit.
Correct lower boundary with an inclusive upper halfway point receives half credit.
